ANELLDR, a loader that has been in use since at least 2018, was designed to decrypt and execute UPPERCUT in memory. ANELLDR can use anti-analysis techniques and is known to share code overlap with HiddenFace.

PHPsert is a webshell used to execute PHP code that has been in use since at least 2023 against targets in Japan, Singapore, Peru, Taiwan, Iran, Republic of Korea, and the Philippines. PHPsert is not typically deployed as a standalone but integrated into web content such as text editors and content management systems.
IronWind is a custom loader malware that has been in use since at least 2023 by actors including WIRTE to target entities in the Middle East.
SameCoin is a multi-platform wiper with Windows and Android versions that has been used by WIRTE to target entities in the Middle East including in Israel.

AshTag is a modular .NET backdoor with multiple features that has been used by WIRTE since at least 2025. AshTag is designed for persistence and remote command execution and can masquerade as a legitimate VisualServer utility.

MuddyViper is custom backdoor written in C and C++ used by MuddyWater for command and control (C2) communications and persistence. MuddyViper is loaded by Fooder and sends frequent messages to the C2 server.

Fooder is a custom 64-bit C/C++ loader used by MuddyWater that can decrypt and reflectively load embedded payloads such as a go-socks5 proxy utility, the open-source HackBrowserData infostealer, or the MuddyViper backdoor. Fooder has frequently masqueraded as an entertainment executable, such as the Snake game (e.g., `Snake_Game.exe`).

Tsundere Botnet is a botnet first reported in mid-2025 that is delivered via MSI installer or a PowerShell script. It leverages Node.js and JavaScript for payload delivery and execution, and uses smart contracts on the blockchain to host command and control (C2) addresses. Tsundere Botnet is attributed to a likely Russian-speaking threat actor.

A variant named DinDoor has been linked to MuddyWater operations and uses the Deno runtime for execution rather than Node.js.

LAMEHUG is Python-based information stealer first identified in July 2025 by Ukraine's Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-UA) in phishing emails targeting Ukrainian government officials. LAMEHUG is the first known malware to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) directly into its attack workflow by querying large language models (LLMs) hosted on Hugging Face to dynamically generate reconnaissance, data theft, and system manipulation commands in real time. LAMEHUG has been attributed to APT28.
LP-Notes is a C/C++ Windows credential stealer used by MuddyWater. LP-Notes was named after the `lp-notes.txt` file that is used to store stolen credentials.

RustyWater is a Rust-based implant used by MuddyWater. Historically, MuddyWater has used PowerShell-based tools and RustyWater reflects a shift in tooling, demonstrating better techniques for defense evasion and reverse engineering.

DynoWiper is a destructive malware associated with the 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks in December of 2025. DynoWiper is a native Windows binary that is distributed by a PowerShell script and overwrites files using data generated by the Mersenne Twister algorithm before they are deleted from the system. Multiple variants of DynoWiper have been identified, with the primary differences being that one variant shuts down the system after completing its destructive operations, and another introduces a time delay between file overwriting and deletion.

LazyWiper is a destructive malware observed targeting a manufacturing sector company during the 2025 Poland Wiper Attacks. LazyWiper is a native Windows PowerShell script that is believed to have been generated by a large language model (LLM). LazyWiper overwrites files on the system using the C# function `WriteRandomBytes()` and can target multiple specific file types by their extensions.

The TeamPCP Cloud Stealer is a comprehensive filesystem credential stealer that can harvest, encrypt, and exfiltrate credentials from over 50 sensitive file paths across CI/CD, cloud, developer tooling, and container environments. The TeamPCP Cloud Stealer was the primary payload used by TeamPCP in March 2026 during early stages of a cascading supply chain campaign targeting CI/CD workflows.

CanisterWorm is a self-propagating malware that has been used by TeamPCP in credential harvesting and software supply chain campaigns since at least 2026. CanisterWorm has used npm credentials to infect software packages and propagate across developer ecosystems. CanisterWorm has a targeted wiper component and can use decentralized C2 infrastructure implemented via an Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) blockchain canister.

Mini Shai-Hulud is a credential stealer and self-replicating supply chain worm, derived from Shai-Hulud, that has been used by TeamPCP to target Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (CI/CD) workflows since at least 2026. Mini Shai-Hulud can compromise credentials across multiple cloud, container, and AI configuration file paths and can use stolen npm and GitHub OIDC tokens to spread to other packages maintained by the compromised user. Mini Shai-Hulud also has a targeted wiper component and has used multiple C2 and data exfiltration mechanisms.

Kali365 is a Phishing-as-a-Service (PHaaS) kit first observed in April 2026 that generates victim-targeted lures across multiple operating systems to induce users into copying and pasting actor-controlled commands for local execution. Kali365 incorporates on-demand device code generation and mirrors the copy-paste execution tradecraft associated with ClickFix. Operators have used Kali365 to harvest victims' OAuth tokens and session cookies through adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) interception, enabling account takeover. Kali365 PHaaS was first observed in April 2026. Kali365 has also been affiliated with other branding to include Octopi365 and Freedom365.

BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR is a 49-module Python malware developed entirely by Anthropic’s Claude Code as part of the AI-Assisted Breach of Mexico's Government Infrastructure campaign. BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR leverages publicly available techniques for network enumeration, credential harvesting, Active Directory interrogation, database access, privilege escalation, cloud metadata extraction, and lateral movement.

IOControl is a malware that targeted Linux ARM-based IoT/OT devices including Hikvision IP cameras, D-Link firewalls and routers, Unitronics PLCs and HMIs, Orpak and Gasboy fuel management systems, and Baicells LTE controllers across the United States and Israel. The malware has been attributed to CyberAv3ngers which is suspected to be affiliated with the Iranian Government Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Vidar is a Windows infostealer that was first advertised in November 2018. Written in C++, Vidar collects PII, cryptocurrency wallets, documents and other data within the compromised machine. Version 2 of Vidar was published in October 2025, and has been used in numerous operations since its release. Vidar has been observed alongside other malware strains, including STOP/Djvu ransomware, Mina.exe (an XMRIG miner), and Clip1.exe (a Laplas Clipper sample).

The Gentlemen Ransomware is a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS). The Gentlemen Ransomware has been written in Go programming language and has utilized Garble to obfuscate its code to target Windows environments. The Gentlemen Ransomware is capable of executing its’ OS lockers in Windows, Linux, NAS, BSD and ESXi environments. The Gentlemen Ransomware was first observed in mid-2025 as a closed ransomware and shortly later emerged as a RaaS to affiliates in September 2025. The Gentlemen Ransomware has been affiliated with the threat group The Gentlemen.

MiniFast is a custom malware designed for long-term persistence and remote code execution. MiniFast is a modular malware suspected of being generated using artificial intelligence (AI). MiniFast was first observed in early-2026 and is a modified version of the MiniJunk framework. MiniFast has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

MiniJunk is a custom malware designed for long-term persistence and remote code execution. MiniJunk  was first observed in 2025 and is a modified version of the MiniBike framework that was first observed in June 2022. MiniJunk has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

CRASHPAD is a Windows executable written in C++ that gathers data from web browsers. CRASHPAD  was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

SIGHTGRAB is a Windows executable written in C that captures and stages stolen data on victim devices. SIGHTGRAB was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

MiniBike is a custom backdoor written in C++ designed for command execution, data discovery, gathering, and exfiltration. MiniBike has been known to communicate with the C2 using Azure Cloud Infrastructure. MiniBike was first observed in 2022. MiniBike has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

MiniBus is a custom backdoor used for command execution, data discovery, gathering, and exfiltration. MiniBus has utilized Azure Cloud Infrastructure and unique adversary-controlled domains for command and control. MiniBus is an updated platform to its predecessor MiniBike and was first observed in August 2023. MiniBus has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

LIGHTRAIL is a tunneler malware. LIGHTRAIL has been known to communicate with C2 SOCKS4A Websocket communications. LIGHTRAIL was first observed in 2022. LIGHTRAIL has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

MiniBrowse is a custom stealer designed for the theft of credentials in browsers and passwords stores. MiniBrowse was first observed in late-2025. MiniBrowse has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

DEEPROOT is a Linux backdoor written in Golang. DEEPROOT is able to execute commands via a shell, enumerate systems, delete or download files, and exfiltrate data. DEEPROOT was first observed in 2025. DEEPROOT has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

TRUSTTRAP is a malware that uses a fictitious prompt to trick users to submit their credentials. TRUSTTRAP was first observed in 2023 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

DCSYNCER.SLICK is a Windows executable that is designed to gather credentials from victim devices. DCSYNCER.SLICK was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

POLLBLEND is a Windows tunneler written C++ that has utilized hardcoded C2 servers and leveraged hardcoded URI parameters for follow-on actions. POLLBLEND was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.

TWOSTROKE is malicious backdoor written in C++ that is capable of discovery actions, executing payloads and exfiltrating data. TWOSTROKE was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group NIMBUS MANTICORE.
